A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GGEUR work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content. v2 adds Appendices D–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification results, component ablations, geometric-similarity analyses and convergence experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds client-scaling and training-time measurements in Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The covariance aggregation, geometry-guided embedding augmentation, CLIP features and cross-domain prototype procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 moves from the main text to the appendix without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, Digits, Office-Caltech, PACS and Office-Home-LDS. The added experiments vary client counts on CIFAR-10 and measure runtime on Digits, without introducing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new scalability and timing evaluations reuse FedAvg, SCAFFOLD and MOON rather than introducing additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds CIFAR-10 evaluations at beta = 0.1 with 100, 300 and 500 clients, supplementing the original ten-client settings. Appendix F adds training-time evaluation, labeled average seconds per round. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused analyses of sensitivity to client count and computational overhead in Appendices E–F. The original augmentation-step ablations, geometric-similarity analysis and convergence comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: The final-five-round averaging and cross-domain standard deviation reporting remain unchanged. The latter measures domain fairness. No seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are newly reported.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark values are unchanged. Table 10 adds GGEUR accuracies of 93.55%, 92.17% and 90.43% for 100, 300 and 500 clients. Table 11 adds per-round overheads of 3.5, 4.6 and 3.3 seconds for FedAvg, SCAFFOLD and MOON. Table 10 prints the 300-client gain as 7.84, although 92.17 minus 84.69 equals 7.48.

T1.justification: Appendix D newly asserts a low-rank covariance condition and develops mathematical privacy arguments based on non-unique reconstruction and aggregation. These do not constitute a formal privacy guarantee. The original definitions, covariance derivation and augmentation equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims about geometry-guided distribution alignment, privacy preservation and effectiveness across label and domain skew.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds explanations asserting that covariance geometry and aggregation prevent reconstruction and isolation of individual client contributions. Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendices E–F additionally interpret the new experiments as evidence of scalability and minimal overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds an access link for the Office-Home-LDS dataset and constructor, and Appendix F supplies training-time measurements. The original code link, optimizer information and hyperparameter tables are retained; timing hardware and accounting details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Appendix D newly invokes 'Melis et al.' to support a comparison between covariance-sharing and gradient-sharing privacy risks, without providing a full reference. The existing related-work discussion and numbered bibliography otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds three short appendix sections, explanatory text after Equation (4), and cross-references to the new analyses. Algorithm 2 is relocated, while the main narrative and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 10–11 are added and Algorithm 2 moves from page 5 to the final appendix page. Several existing figures are rasterized and surrounding content reflows, while their scientific content and the existing table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices E–F add useful, focused evidence on scalability and runtime, while the dataset/constructor link improves reproducibility documentation. These modest gains are tempered by Table 10's incorrect 300-client gain, ambiguous timing scope, and Appendix D's unsupported blanket privacy assertions.
